Done. Both deliverables are in place at `out/骨架.md` and `out/structure.json`.

**What I built.** The skeleton is a 45-second vertical short-video storyboard for 露营灯选购, structured as a four-stage viral formula: 反常识钩子 (0–3s) → 痛点共鸣 (3–8s) → 三点干货 (8–38s) → 清单收束 + CTA (38–45s). It breaks into 6 shots (S1–S6), and your three points land one per shot as S3/S4/S5, each carrying an evidence-shot description, a boundary condition, and an explicit "禁" (what not to say on camera) — that's what keeps the piece from reading as a flat parameter list.

Each shot row specifies shot size, what to actually film, a voiceover line, on-screen caption text, an edit note, and the structural role it plays. The arguments are: 3500K warm white against 6500K cold white on the same dish in a split-screen; a calculator graphic showing 8h rated ÷ 2 = ~4h real; and a single-take magnet-stick-then-hook-throw at a tree branch so the light stays on. It also ships title candidates, cover spec, hashtags, a BGM curve that drops a half-beat of silence at 00:08 and 00:28 to land the arguments, a publish window, and comment-ops copy.

**Verification.** `structure.json` is an exact mirror of the Markdown, and I checked that programmatically rather than by eye: the timeline is contiguous from 00:00 to 00:45 with no gaps, the duration fields sum to 45 (3+5+10+10+10+7), all three of your points appear verbatim in both files, and every shot field, title, and hashtag in the JSON was located in the Markdown. All 90+ assertions passed.

One note on scope: the `fixtures/` directory in this arm is empty and `arms_manifest.json` records `baseline_has_skill: false`, so I generated the skeleton from the brief alone without a skill or template to conform to — hence the self-declared `baseline-v1` version marker in both files.
